QuarticQuery.AdaptiveProgram.doc_comment: Finite classical control over unitary steps, oracle calls and binary projective measurements. Computation between queries is unrestricted.

QuarticQuery.AdaptiveProgram.outputMass.doc_comment: Branch states stay unnormalised; a branch's probability is its squared norm.

QuarticQuery.AdaptiveProgram.queryCap.doc_comment: The query cap is syntactic: it bounds every branch on every input, including inputs outside a promise.

QuarticQuery.BansalSinhaLower.doc_comment: The external input of Lemma 2.1(i): the Bansal–Sinha randomized lower bound for exactly this `P`, in exactly this query model. It is used as a named hypothesis and is never an axiom.

primary_gloss.excerpt: **The partial function and its domain.** For a finite coordinate type $I$, a formal [partial Boolean function][def-partial] on $I$ is a function from [bit inputs][def-bit-input] on $I$ to optional Boolean values. A defined value records both membership in the promise and the required answer. An undefined value imposes no correctness requirement. This is the domain-and-value description of §2.1, with no assumption of totality. [Totalisation][def-totalise] embeds a total Boolean function into this type by defining its value everywhere. It is that embedding, rather than an arbitrary completion of a partial function, which appears in the total-function separation statements.

QuarticQuery.BitLoc.doc_comment: The four kinds of input bit: the strings `X_i`; the strings `A_{i,h}`; the pointer bits of each cell; the transcript bits of each cell.

primary_gloss.excerpt:
The predicate $D_{\leq}(f,q)$, the [deterministic budget test][def-DLe] of the formal statement, means that there is one tree $T$ of depth at most $q$ with $T(x)=f(x)$ for every $x\in\mathcal D$. Define

\[
D(f)=\min\{q\in\mathbb N:D_{\leq}(f,q)\}.
\]

A randomized program is a finite list of trees $T_1,\ldots,T_s$ with real weights $p_j>0$ and $\sum_jp_j=1$. It selects $j$ independently of the input and runs $T_j$. Its depth is $\max_j\operatorname{depth}(T_j)$, and its success probability on a promised input is $\sum_{j:T_j(x)=f(x)}p_j$. Positive weights merely discard entries of probability zero; the normalization forces $s\geq1$.

primary_gloss.excerpt:
On a nonempty coordinate set, a budget $q$ is admissible when one normalized starting state and one program of cap at most $q$ achieve the required success on every promised input. To include the empty coordinate set, where a constant answer needs no query register, we also allow the constant case explicitly. The resulting condition, the [quantum budget test][def-QLe] of the formal statement, is

\[
\begin{split}
&\bigl[\exists b\in\{0,1\}\ \forall x\in\mathcal D,\ f(x)=b\bigr]\\
&\quad\lor\
\bigl[\exists w,\psi_0,A:\ \|\psi_0\|=1,\
  \operatorname{cap}(A)\leq q,\
  \forall x\in\mathcal D,\ M_A(x,\psi_0,f(x))\geq2/3\bigr].
\end{split}
\]

Every existential choice in the second clause precedes the input quantifier. The first clause permits a constant answer with no query register. It is redundant when a nonempty query register is available, but necessary for the source representation when $I=\varnothing$: there is then one possible input and no unit vector in the zero-dimensional indexed query space. Every partial Boolean function on that singleton input set is constant on its promise, including an empty promise. The clause therefore supplies exactly the expected zero-query behavior.

Define $Q(f)=\min\{q\in\mathbb N:\text{`QLe f q'}\}$. To see that this minimum exists, simulate a deterministic tree. On a nonempty coordinate set, prepare the basis state for its next query with answer bit zero, query once, measure the answer bit, and follow the corresponding child. Each child has its own input-independent basis permutation preparing its next coordinate. The classical history is already encoded by the program branch. Induction on the tree gives the same output and no larger cap. Constant trees, including those on empty coordinates, use the first clause. Hence

\[
Q(f)\leq D(f)\leq |I|,
\qquad
Q(f)\leq q\iff\text{`QLe f q'}.
\]

As in the classical case, nonemptiness and monotonicity of admissible budgets justify the source's natural-number infimum.

primary_gloss.excerpt:
Write $R_{\leq}(f,q)$ for the existence of such a mixture with depth at most $q$ and success at least $2/3$ on every promised input; this is the [randomized budget test][def-RLe] of the formal statement. The randomized complexity is

\[
R(f)=\min\left\{q\in\mathbb N:\
\exists(p_j,T_j)_{j=1}^s\quad
\begin{array}{l}
p_j>0,\quad \sum_jp_j=1,\quad \operatorname{depth}(T_j)\leq q\ \text{for every }j,\\[2pt]
\displaystyle \sum_{j:T_j(x)=f(x)}p_j\geq\frac23\ \text{for every }x\in\mathcal D
\end{array}\right\}.
\]

This is the distribution-over-trees convention in [Buhrman and de Wolf, §§3.1–3.2, printed pp. 5–6][BDW02]. For fixed $I$ and $q$, there are finitely many trees of depth at most $q$: at depth zero there are two leaves, and a larger tree chooses a coordinate and two smaller trees. Fixing all random choices of a capped randomized algorithm selects one such tree; grouping outcomes that select the same tree gives a finite mixture. Conversely, a finite distribution can be selected with finitely many biased coin choices before reading the input. These observations preserve the cap and pointwise success probabilities. They use the allowed arbitrary real biases; a separate restriction to a bounded number of fair coin flips requires care at an exact error threshold.

The minima exist. Query all coordinates once, then output the prescribed value on the promise and any bit elsewhere. This tree has depth at most $|I|$, including when $I$ is empty. A tree is also a one-element randomized mixture. The admissible budgets are therefore nonempty upward-closed subsets of $\mathbb N$, giving

\[
R(f)\leq q\iff R_{\leq}(f,q),\qquad
D(f)\leq q\iff D_{\leq}(f,q),\qquad
R(f)\leq D(f)\leq |I|.
\]

**Formal representation.** In the source these minima are natural-number infima. The read-all witness is what makes them minima of nonempty sets; the value assigned to an empty infimum does no work. The constructor-by-constructor translation to the decision trees of complexitylib preserves both evaluation and depth, and for total functions it gives the [exact equality of the two deterministic complexities][src-complexitylib].

\neg\exists C\in\mathbb R\ \forall n\geq1\

R(F_{k,m})\geq c_k\frac{m^{2-1/k}}{(\log_2 m)^2}.

primary_gloss.excerpt:
$$
a_{i^\star j}\geq1-\varepsilon\qquad(j\ne i^\star).
$$

The proof uses the correctness of the true winner's decoder and two deterministic facts: the winner cannot be disqualified, and its true-address pointers disqualify every opponent. Nothing is assumed about a nonwinning column's decoder. This is also why amplifying an assumed comparison bias would be unjustified: the available guarantee is a strong one-sided property of a true winner, while other pairs may have arbitrary probabilities.

primary_gloss.excerpt: **One algorithm and a global cap.** The [deterministic][def-DLe], [randomized][def-RLe] and [quantum][def-QLe] budget tests take a partial Boolean function and a natural-number budget; the complexities [$D$][def-D], [$R$][def-R] and [$Q$][def-Q] are natural numbers. > For every input y and (i,s) in [m] x {0,1}^r: i wins at s iff all K_{k,m} tests pass, namely (a) X_i[b]=1 for each b; (b) for each j != i, X_j[p_{i,s,j}]=0; (c) for each h and each non-input gate, the claimed value equals the gate function of its predecessors, read from the transcript or from A_{i,h}; (d) for each h, claimed d=1 and claimed b=s_h. Each test is computed by a deterministic adaptive bit-query decision tree of depth at most max(3,l+1), which is l+1 for m>=4: a pointer test reads l pointer bits, then the one target bit they select, while gate tests read at most three fixed bits. A pointer test is not a function of a small fixed set of bits: it can depend on all l+m pointer and target coordinates.

primary_gloss.excerpt: **The partial function and its domain.** For a finite coordinate type $I$, a formal [partial Boolean function][def-partial] on $I$ is a function from [bit inputs][def-bit-input] on $I$ to optional Boolean values. A defined value records both membership in the promise and the required answer. An undefined value imposes no correctness requirement. This is the domain-and-value description of §2.1, with no assumption of totality. [Totalisation][def-totalise] embeds a total Boolean function into this type by defining its value everywhere. It is that embedding, rather than an arbitrary completion of a partial function, which appears in the total-function separation statements.

In the quantum case, the witness is either the explicitly constant-on-promise alternative or one normalized initial state and one capped program, chosen before the input. This includes the constant and empty-promise cases without selecting an algorithm separately for each input. None of these definitions assumes a lower-bound theorem or any property of Forrelation.

primary_gloss.excerpt: **The family and the universal exponent.** The [universal power bound][def-universal] is a predicate on real exponents, and the [formal optimal exponent][def-alpha] is the infimum of the exponents satisfying it. Its quantifiers range over total Boolean functions on $\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, with $n\ge1$ and exponent $\alpha\ge0$, as in (1). The finite-constant and infimum formulations are explicitly related by the source wrappers. No Forrelation hypothesis belongs to this definition.

The ordinary fresh-trial/routing argument in §5.6 supplies the mathematical construction. The round-four integration added the [amplifier for opaque preparations][cmp-amplifier], accepted by Comparator: for one selector gate chosen before every opaque unitary, it states the retained-factor identity and the exact success mass, with the zero-mass, $p/2$ and $1-\eta$ clauses and a logical cap. The basis change from a general fixed projector to a coordinate predicate and the literal flag/Hadamard identification remain unproved, so no source-bound Lean theorem of the full physical type displayed above is claimed. In particular, the coherent composition can retain a copy of a successful output label in auxiliary registers, and the measured compilation route reads a complete basis label. What remains is the physical transport and uncomputation statement: after the chosen compiler and any copied labels, the designated physical output subsystem must still have the abstract successful factor $g_x$. The accepted opaque identity alone does not identify that subsystem. This bridge is needed before promoting the physical wrapper to the full state claim. This missing formal bridge is not an extra assumption in the proof of Proposition 3.3: that proof uses only measured labels, whose law is already supplied by the compiled route.

primary_gloss.excerpt:
The round-four integration added the
[direct product on the cap event][cmp-direct-product] as an endpoint, accepted by
Comparator. It covers a finite seed space with arbitrary nonnegative weights
summing to one, each seed selecting an initially uncapped tree, and bounds the
weighted joint event that every instance is answered correctly and no
instance exceeds its cap of $L$ queries by $\beta^r$. [Compliance with the caps][src-complies] is
a recursive predicate, which follows the path taken on the
given input and decrements the cap of each queried instance. The observable
[query count][src-count], the number of queries that path makes to each instance,
is defined separately, and the equivalence of the two descriptions is not a
Lean theorem.
